quote: The stomodeum is beginning to form.
note: The table starts the stomodeum at CS10; the source has it beginning to form at CS9. One stage early.

quote: The stomodeum is beginning to form.
note: The table starts the hindgut at CS10. At CS9 the source already has it 'making its appearance as a separate' region in some specimens, though combined with the midgut in others -- so CS9 is where it becomes distinguishable and CS10 is a stage late. Note the specimen-dependence: this is a transition, not a point.

quote: Although a sinus venosus as such is not present until the next stage, left and right sinusal horns appear during stage 10.
note: Confirms the table's CS10 start exactly: 'The thyroid primordium appears'.

quote: Internal: septum primum and foramen primum appear in the heart; right and left lung buds are recognizable, and the trachea begins its development; retinal and lens discs appear; the endolymphatic appendage becomes distinguishable by the end of the stage.
note: Confirms the table's CS13 start, and names the pouch it derives from.

quote: Internal: the interventricular septum has begun; the cystic primordium and the dorsal pancreas are becoming distinguishable; the lung bud appears.
note: Confirms the table's CS12 start: the stage summary says the lung bud appears. Note the source separately tracks a 'pulmonary primordium' from CS10, so a curator who treats those as the same structure would want CS10 instead -- the table's reading is defensible but not the only one.

quote: The embryo is presomitic, i.e., somites are not yet visible.
note: Brackets the table's CS9 start from below, and the stage-9 characteristic feature is '1-3 pairs of somites'. Presomitic at CS8, somites at CS9: the bound is exactly right.

quote: Characteristic features: implanted but previllous; solid trophoblast in 5a; trophoblastic lacunae, cytotrophoblastic clumps, and primary umbilical vesicle in 5b; lacunar vascular circle and some mesoblastic crests in cytotrophoblastic clumps in 5c
note: Brackets the table's CS6 start from below: stage 5 is defined as previllous. Stage 6's characteristic feature is 'chorionic villi ... in 6a'. The bound is exactly right.

quote: Additional features of stage 5 include the definite appearance of the amniotic cavity and the formation of extra-embryonic mesoblast.
note: Confirms the table's CS5 start: the definite appearance of the amniotic cavity is listed among the features of stage 5.

quote: The stomodeum is beginning to form.
note: Confirms the table's CS9 start, with a useful caveat in the same sentence: the region can be made out at CS9 although no nephric structures are found until CS10. The CS10 summary says it 'becomes visible', so CS9 is the earliest defensible bound rather than a comfortable one.

quote: Internal: the sinus venosus develops; the oropharyngeal membrane ruptures; the mesonephric duct and nephric tubules appear; the optic vesicle and otic pit develop.
note: Confirms the table's CS11 start: the stage summary lists the optic vesicle developing.

quote: Internal: septum primum and foramen primum appear in the heart; right and left lung buds are recognizable, and the trachea begins its development; retinal and lens discs appear; the endolymphatic appendage becomes distinguishable by the end of the stage.
note: Confirms the table's CS13 start: the beginning of an optic cup can be seen at this stage.

quote: Internal: septum primum and foramen primum appear in the heart; right and left lung buds are recognizable, and the trachea begins its development; retinal and lens discs appear; the endolymphatic appendage becomes distinguishable by the end of the stage.
note: Confirms the table's CS13 start: CS13 is where both upper and lower limb buds are first visible. The same sentence bears on forelimb bud, which the table starts at CS12 -- the source says stage 12 has 'either no upper limb bud at all, or in the oldest members of the group a representative of it in the form of a slight elevation', so the CS12 bound is specimen-dependent and weaker than the CS13 one.

quote: Although a sinus venosus as such is not present until the next stage, left and right sinusal horns appear during stage 10.
note: Confirms the table's CS10 start. The same sentence hedges the maxillary process ('probably'), which the table starts at CS13 -- three stages later than a hedged first mention, so that bound deserves a look.

quote: The cerebellar plate (innerer Kleinhirnwulst of Hochsetter) is present as a clear thickening.
note: The table starts the chondrocranium at CS16; the source's first mention is 'the beginning chondrocranium' at CS17. One stage early.

quote: Internal: the interventricular septum has begun; the cystic primordium and the dorsal pancreas are becoming distinguishable; the lung bud appears.
note: Contradicts the table directly. The table starts pharyngeal arch 4 at CS12, but CS12's characteristic feature is three pharyngeal arches, 'in contrast with the two of the previous stage'. Three arches at CS12 means the fourth is not yet there. The bound must move later.

quote: Although a sinus venosus as such is not present until the next stage, left and right sinusal horns appear during stage 10.
note: Confirms the table's CS10 start: cleft 2 and pouch 2 are identifiable at CS10. The same sentence hedges pouch 3 ('may be indicated'), which the table starts at CS11 -- consistent.
